name: showreel-34-press

voice.text: Why does your button feel dead on tap? You tap, nothing moves, so you tap again. The fix: scale it to ninety six percent while it's pressed, with a quick transition. Now every tap feels like a real press.

caption:
Why does your button feel dead on tap? 👆

With no :active style, a tap gives no sign it landed, so people tap again (and pay twice). Give the button a transition on scale and shrink it to 96% while it is pressed: every tap now feels like a real press. On iPhone, Safari only shows :active when the page listens for touches, so add ontouchstart to your <body>. Works in Chrome 104+, Safari 14.1+ and Firefox 72+ (or use transform: scale(.96) for older browsers).
Save it for your next button, or send it to whoever built your checkout.

sources.note: MDN :active: matches an element while it is being activated (pressed) by the user; BCD css.selectors.active: all browsers; safari_ios note: by default Safari on iOS does not use :active unless there is a touchstart handler on the element or on <body> (read from mdn/browser-compat-data 12 Nov 2026)
MDN scale (the individual transform property); BCD css.properties.scale: Chrome 104, Firefox 72, Safari 14.1 (iOS mirror)

tip.title: Why does your button feel dead on tap?
tip.why: A button with no :active style gives no sign a tap landed, so people tap again. A short transition on scale and scale: .96 while :active make it dip under the finger and spring back (MDN :active, scale). Safari on iOS only applies :active when the page has a touchstart listener, so add ontouchstart to <body> (BCD note).
